title: kit.broker-config.v1
description: One project's agent credential broker (@saasreport/broker, docs/BROKER.md): which GitHub App it acts as, which repositories it serves, which agents may ask for what, and what a merge requires. Agents hold no GitHub credential; they sign requests with their own Ed25519 key.

project.description: The project code from the registry (packages/core/registry/projects.json).

id.description: The GitHub App id (not secret). The private key is the Worker secret APP_PRIVATE_KEY and never appears in config.

owner.description: The organisation the app is installed on.

repos.description: Repositories (under app.owner) the broker serves. A token is always scoped to exactly one of them.

publicKey.description: The agent's own Ed25519 public key (raw 32 bytes, canonical base64). One key per agent, never shared.

reviewer.description: May sign the independent review a merge requires. A reviewer holds no write action and not merge (the Worker refuses the config otherwise), so it can never review its own work.

actions.description: Token actions: the GitHub permissions the installation token for that action carries. `merge` is not a token action; the broker merges itself. Workflows is not offered at all (GitHub has no read level for it, and an agent never writes workflows through the broker).

checks.description: Never write: an agent must not be able to create the check runs the merge gate trusts.

statuses.description: Never write, for the same reason.

actions.description: Never write: re-running or dispatching workflows is not an agent's to do.

reviewMaxAgeSeconds.description: How old the signed review may be when the merge is asked for. The head pin makes an older review useless anyway; this bounds how long a review can wait.

requiredChecks.description: Check runs that must each be present on the head, completed, with an allowed conclusion, created by the named GitHub App (e.g. 15368 for GitHub Actions). Runs created by this broker's own app never count. Every other run present must also be completed and allowed, and the combined commit status must not be pending or failing.

allowedBases.description: Base branches the broker merges into. The review signs the base, so a base changed after the review is refused.

freshnessSeconds.description: How old (or how far in the future) a signed request may be.
